feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. The evidence is iterations 0 to 4. Iteration 1 (0.8 kg, widened 12 mm row, wheel_track 0.12 m, score 324.07) is the reference: oval finish rate 0.70, oval steering_oscillation 0.26. Iteration 4 (0.6 kg, same geometry and controller, score 247.82) cut oval finishes to 0.30 and raised oscillation to 0.32, so the lighter robot is losing grip rather than gaining turn response. Iteration 3 (wheel_track 0.10 m, kp 4.5) also cut oval finishes, to 0.10, so shorter track is not the fix. Iteration 2 (16 mm sensors) collapsed oval finishes to 0.00, so keep 12 mm. The mass 0.7 kg candidate is a sensible midpoint test. Depending on the next race: if oval finishes return to about 0.5 or more with oscillation at or below about 0.3, hold mass at 0.7 kg. If finishes stay near 0.3 while mass 0.7 kg is no better than 0.6 kg, treat it as noise and return to 0.8 kg, the best known mass. Do not move the sensors or the track again, because the evidence for those is already used up.
requested_changes: If oval finish rate at 0.7 kg is about 0.5 or more with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.3, hold mass at 0.7 kg and keep the rest of the geometry fixed (iteration 4 showed mass 0.6 kg loses grip).
If the oval finish rate at 0.7 kg stays near 0.3 or below, return to mass 0.8 kg, the iteration 1 best (oval finish 0.70), and do not try a lower mass again.
Do not change sensor_size or reduce wheel_track below 0.12 m. Iteration 2 (16 mm sensors) and iteration 3 (0.10 m track) both hurt the oval finish rate.
